items.description: Sec. 4 (and Abstract) give only '16 × 32 square elements' for a cantilever; which count runs along the beam axis (length) and which through the depth is not stated. The domain shape is visible only in Figs. 10–12, which are unavailable.
readings: 32 elements along the cantilever axis × 16 elements deep (length:height = 2:1)
16 elements along the cantilever axis × 32 elements deep (length:height = 1:2)

items.entity: physical element size and out-of-plane thickness
items.description: Only element counts are given; element edge length and plate thickness are never stated (Sec. 4 says units were omitted). In a 2-D model with nodal loads, element size does not change compliance and thickness scales it as 1/t.
readings: unit square elements (edge 1) and unit thickness
other edge length and/or thickness t ≠ 1

items.description: Sec. 4 says only 'As the boundary condition, we choose the cantilever' (Conclusion: 'a cantilever beam'). It does not say which edge is fixed, or whether all of its nodes or only discrete points are restrained (Sec. 3.2.1 mentions 'the support point'). Any sketch would be in the unavailable figures.
readings: entire left short edge (all nodes) fixed, free end at the opposite right edge
only discrete nodes of the left edge fixed (e.g., its two end nodes)
entire 32-element side fixed (if the domain is read as 16 long × 32 deep)

items.description: 'Cantilever' suggests clamping, but the text never says which displacement components are restrained at the support nodes.
readings: clamped: ux = uy = 0 at every support node
ux = 0 at all support nodes, uy = 0 at a single node only

items.entity: point of load application at the free end
items.description: No load location is given anywhere (Sec. 4, Conclusion). 'Cantilever' implies a load on the free edge but not where along it.
readings: mid-height node of the free (right) edge
bottom corner node of the free edge (top corner is the mirror-equivalent)

items.description: The text does not say whether the load is a single nodal force or spread over several nodes or the whole edge.
readings: single nodal point force
force shared by a few adjacent nodes around the load point
uniform shear traction over the whole free edge

items.description: Load direction is never stated; 'cantilever' implies a transverse load. In this linear problem the sign alone does not matter, but a component along the beam axis would change the result.
readings: vertical (transverse) downward
vertical (transverse) upward — identical layout and compliance
inclined, with a component along the beam axis

items.description: No load value is given. The 'dimensionless' compliances in Table 3 (initial 5,974, SIMP 1,294, proposed 1,287) scale with F², so they cannot be matched without it.
readings: F = 1 (unit load)
F scaled so that the uniform initial design gives C = 5,974

items.description: Sec. 4 states ν = 1.0, which is not valid for isotropic linear elasticity: the plane-stress factor E/(1−ν²) is singular at ν = 1, and plane strain or 3-D needs ν < 0.5. This is almost certainly a typo or text-extraction error.
Plane stress vs. plane strain is not stated; the text mentions only FEM with square elements.
readings: plane stress
plane strain

items.description: Element formulation and integration are not given. Sec. 3.2.4 blames checkerboards on shear locking, which suggests low-order quadrilaterals.
readings: 4-node bilinear quad (Q4), full 2×2 Gauss integration
Q4 with reduced/selective integration or incompatible modes
8-node quadratic quad

items.entity: lower density bound xmin / void stiffness
items.description: Eqs. (3)–(4) introduce xmin 'to eliminate numerical instability' but give no value. The text also does not say what stiffness the 0-elements from Eq. (7) receive when the compliances of the filtered designs (Table 3) are evaluated.
readings: xmin = 0.001 (thresholded voids also set to xmin)
xmin = 0.01
near-zero void stiffness (e.g., 1e-9·E0)

items.description: The move limit m appears in the OC update Eq. (5) and in the Nomenclature, but its value is not given.
The damping coefficient η (Nomenclature; exponent in the OC update, Eqs. (5)–(6)) is not given.

items.entity: sensitivity/density filter in the SIMP-OC loop (previous method)
items.description: For the previous method, Sec. 2.3 describes only post-processing (threshold Eq. (7) and floating-island removal). No mesh-independence or anti-checkerboard sensitivity/density filter, and no radius, is mentioned. Fig. 12(a) is called raw OC data 'without filtering'.
readings: no sensitivity or density filter
sensitivity filter with rmin = 1.5 elements
sensitivity or density filter with rmin = 2 elements

items.description: Sec. 2.4 step 5 iterates until the change in x falls below 'a certain value', which is not given. The Fig. 11 caption and Table 2, however, report results after a fixed 40 density updates. It is unclear whether 40 was a cap or the point of convergence.
readings: exactly 40 OC updates
until max|x_new − x| < 0.01
until max|x_new − x| < 0.001

items.description: The threshold has no numerical value. Sec. 2.3 defines it only as the value that makes the SIMP volume after filtering close to the volume of the filtered CNN-TO result, and that volume is not reported.
readings: threshold = 0.5
threshold giving 50% solid elements (256 of 512)
threshold matching the unreported post-filter volume of the CNN-TO design

items.description: Sec. 2.4 step 6 and Sec. 3.2 step 6 apply filtering once, after convergence. But Sec. 5.2.1 blames a compliance rise near update 30 in Fig. 13(b) on the filtering, which implies filters act during the iterations. Sec. 3.2.3 also speaks of filtering 'with the optimum structure generated by the CNN as the initial structure'.
readings: filters applied once to the final (40th-update) design only
filters applied after every OC update and fed back into the loop
filters applied at an intermediate stage (e.g., ≈ update 30), then OC continued from the filtered design

items.description: Floating islands are elements 'not connected to any other elements regarded as material' (Sec. 3.2.4.1, also used for the previous method per Sec. 2.3). The text does not specify: edge vs. corner connectivity; whether whole clusters cut off from the supported body are removed; or the order relative to thresholding.
readings: remove only single solid elements with no solid neighbour among their 8 neighbours
remove every solid cluster not edge-connected (4-connectivity) to the support-connected main body
as above but with 8-connectivity (corner contact counts as connected)

items.description: Sec. 4 describes the initial design as 'an evenly distributed density over the design area (see Fig. 10)'. Its numerical value appears only in the unavailable figure. Table 3's initial-to-optimal compliance ratio (≈4.6) is plausible for 0.5 with p = 3.
readings: uniform x = 0.5 (equal to the volume fraction)
another uniform value (e.g., 0.4 or 0.6)

items.entity: volume of the final filtered designs (Fig. 11(b),(d), Table 3)
items.description: The 50% upper limit (Sec. 4) governs the OC iterations. However, the threshold is tuned to match the two methods' volumes rather than 50% (Sec. 2.3), and hole filling may violate the mass constraint (Sec. 3.2.4). The volumes of the filtered designs compared in Table 3 are not reported.
readings: filtered designs re-adjusted to exactly 50% (256 of 512 elements solid)
filtered designs left at whatever volume filtering produces (unreported, possibly ≠ 50%)

items.description: Sec. 3.2.4.2 fills holes smaller than 'a certain size', which is never given. Sec. 3.2.4 also says one 'should check' for checkerboards before filling, but gives no rule for this.
readings: fill only single-element holes
fill holes up to 4 elements (2×2)
fill holes up to 9 elements (3×3)

items.description: The criterion is given (≤ 2 solid among 8 neighbours, Sec. 3.2.4.3). Unspecified: how edge/corner elements with fewer than 8 neighbours are treated; single vs. repeated passes; and order relative to island removal and hole filling.
readings: single pass, out-of-domain neighbours counted as void
repeat until no element qualifies, out-of-domain neighbours counted as void
out-of-domain neighbours counted as solid or ignored

items.description: The island, hole and peninsula filters of Sec. 3.2.4 require classifying the continuous OC densities as solid or void. No threshold is given for the proposed method; Eq. (7) is attributed only to the previous method (Appendix 1).
readings: threshold 0.5
same threshold as Eq. (7)
only elements at the upper bound x = 1 counted as material

items.description: Fig. 11(c),(d) rely on sensitivities estimated by a CNN, but Table 1 lists only strides and channel counts. Missing: kernel sizes, padding, activations, loss, size of the final fully connected layer, training-set size, bar-system parameters, epochs, batch size and output normalization. Random initial weights also give different optima (CNN 1 vs. CNN 2, Sec. 5.3.2). This part cannot be reproduced with a standard FE-based solver.
readings: reproduce only the SIMP/OC reference (Fig. 11(a),(b)) with exact FE adjoint sensitivities
